card.name: Corrected or adjusted for a variable
card.fires_on: The word "for" (or "corrected"/"adjusted") right after "corrected" or "adjusted", just before the thing being accounted for, such as albumin, heart rate or body weight.

modes.label: Corrected/adjusted for
modes.description: The word "for" after corrected or adjusted, before a correction factor in lab or ECG values.
modes.example: QT QTc = QT interval<< corrected>> for heart rate interval greater than 5

modes.label: Correct for in other settings
modes.description: The verb "correct" or "corrected" itself, or "for" after it, in rates or measurements adjusted for something.
modes.example: The cumulative rates correct the crude rate of 0.7% (25 of 3,519 patients)<< for>> the variable duration of exposure in clinical trials

card.writes: It favors words about approximation and adjustment, though the effect is weak.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a value is said to be corrected or adjusted for something like heart rate or albumin.
